settings.heading: Breakages, first year
settings.text: Replaced from the next firing, free. Photograph it and write; we do not ask you to post the pieces back.

settings.heading: Completing a set
settings.text: Tell us the number cut into the foot and we will match the glaze as closely as a wood kiln allows — and say honestly how close that is.

settings.heading: Repairs in gold
settings.text: Quoted first. A clean break can be joined with gold rather than hidden, which is the older and better answer.

settings.heading: What does the number on the foot mean?
settings.text: The firing, then the piece within it. No. 14/06 is the sixth piece out of the fourteenth firing, and it is recorded against your order.

settings.heading: Can these go in the dishwasher?
settings.text: All four glazes, every day. Only iron black stays out of the microwave, because the iron in the glaze heats.

settings.heading: The glaze has crazed. Is that a fault?
settings.text: No. Fine lines in an ash glaze are normal and do not go through the body. A piece that leaks is a fault, and we replace it.

settings.heading: Can you match a piece I bought years ago?
settings.text: The form, yes. The glaze, not exactly — it came out of a different kiln. We will show you what the current firing looks like before you decide.

settings.heading: Living with it
settings.intro: The practical part. Anything not here, write to us and a person answers.

settings.heading: Ask about a piece
settings.intro: Tell us the number on the foot and what happened. We reply within two working days.
